claim: The lag-trained court-dance tracking policy, exported for deployment (mjlab's tracking ONNX, its reference and a manifest) and driven by the manifest alone in plain MuJoCo, danced to the clip's end in 32 of 40 gate trials under its evaluation's conditions (pushes, observation noise, start-up draws, a per-trial lag in [0, 20] ms), exact 95% interval [0.64, 0.91], against 30 of 40, [0.59, 0.87], in mjlab: the gate passed (its rate within 0.10 of the evaluation's, whose lower bound is above zero). All 19 trials with no lag succeeded; the 8 failures were all one 20 ms tick late, 7 on an end effector's height and 1 on the torso's. Before the gate, the plain runtime's observation terms were checked against mjlab's own on mjlab's rollout states: every term within 2e-6 over 300 ticks, and the tracking bounds fired on the same tick, on the same bound, as mjlab's terminations on two falls.
instrument: WSL2 (Linux 6.18.58.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2), CPU; the export in mjlab-1.6.0+mujoco-3.13.0+warp-1.17.0+cpu (trainnr_mjlab.tracking_export), the gate in mujoco-3.11.0 + onnxruntime (trainnr.deploy.tracking through trainnr.deploy.gate)

verdict.rule: the gate's success rate is at least the evaluation's minus the tolerance, and the evaluation's lower bound is above zero

bounds.zero_actions: mjlab ee_body_pos at tick 9, the plain runtime end effector height at tick 9
bounds.random_actions_x3: mjlab ee_body_pos at tick 19, the plain runtime end effector height at tick 19

parity_with_mjlab.found_on_the_way: the reference's clock leads the control tick by one (mjlab advances it once at reset, from the start pose at frame 0), and the actor's joint_pos term reads the encoder-biased angles; before both were carried, the command term differed by up to 3.8 and joint_pos by 0.0098

artifacts.deploy/court-dance-g1: in the g1-dance test project: policy.onnx (mjlab's tracking export, inputs obs and time_step), motion.npz, deploy.json (trainnr-deploy/1 with its tracking section), scene.xml, assets/ (the G1's meshes from mjlab's asset zoo), gate.json, the gate's saved stream and poses

protocol: Export: export_deployment's tracking route, the evaluation above cited. Gate: gate_deployment on the plain MuJoCo runtime, 40 trials, seed 1000, each trial's draw from (seed, trial): the start drawn around the clip's first frame as training drew it, the encoder bias, the torso's centre of mass and the feet's shared friction drawn once, uniform observation noise per term, pushes at training's intervals and velocities, a lag of 0 or 1 control ticks; the conditions taken from the cited evaluation's protocol. A trial succeeds when the clip plays to its end with none of mjlab's three tracking bounds broken. Parity: mjlab's play-mode rollout of the same checkpoint on one world (no noise, no pushes), its states written into the plain runtime tick by tick and every actor term compared; the bounds compared on falls under zero and random actions with mjlab's auto-reset off.
caveats: The gate's trials are not paired with the evaluation's: both draw their lags from seed 1000 but by different rules (the gate per trial, the evaluation as one vector), and the simulators draw pushes and noise their own ways. The comparison is of rates, within the stated tolerance.
The gate runs core trainnr's MuJoCo (3.11), the evaluation mjlab's MuJoCo Warp (3.13): two simulators, and the agreement is within that difference, not despite it.
With no lag the gate succeeded in 19 of 19 where the evaluation had 15 of 19; whether plain MuJoCo is kinder to this policy or the draws differed is not separated here.
Simulation only: no G1 to deploy to (docs/86 §9). The ONNX is mjlab's own format, which BeyondMimic's motion-tracking controller runs on a G1; that controller was not run.
